- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Succulents are low-maintenance and can add a touch of elegance to any room.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overwatering is the most common cause of death in succulents; it's better to err on the side of caution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Before watering succulents, check the soil by sticking a finger into the soil about an inch deep.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Succulents need bright, indirect light; avoid direct sunlight to prevent scorching.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Most succulents thrive in temperatures between 65°F to 75°F (18°C to 24°C).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Succulents prefer dry air and do not require humidifying.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During the growing season (spring and summer), fertilize succulents with a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer diluted to half the recommended strength.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Choose a well-draining potting mix to prevent waterlogged soil and root rot.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Repot succulents as needed, typically every 1-3 years, using a slightly larger pot with fresh potting mix.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Prune succulents to maintain their shape and encourage new growth; propagation can be done from cuttings.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended beginner-friendly succulents include Aloe Vera, Echeveria, Crassula (Jade Plant), Sedum, Kalanchoe, Peperomia, and certain Cacti.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When selecting succulents, look for healthy plants with plump, firm leaves and avoid those with signs of overwatering.
